whose

Because
Despite
So that

examined
examines
examining

highest

so much
such a
very many

studies

be
has

continued
continues
will continue

has

has fallen
is falling

Despite
Even though
However

smoked
smoking
to smoke

were
will be

very

despite

do
does
is

took

seen
to see

which

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about sleep and memory.
clips.script: Most of us think of sleep as a time when the brain simply switches off. In fact, the opposite is closer to the truth. During deep sleep, the brain replays the events of the day and moves important information from short-term memory into long-term storage. That's why students who stay up all night before an exam often remember less, not more, than those who get a full night's rest.

qs.q: What is the speaker's main point?

o: The brain is completely inactive during sleep.
Students should study only early in the morning.
Sleep helps the brain store new information.
Short-term memory is more important than long-term memory.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between a student and a professor during office hours.

Man: Professor Adams, do you have a minute? It's about the research paper that's due on Friday.

Man: Well, I've collected all my survey data, but about a third of the responses came back incomplete. I'm not sure whether I should include them or throw them out.
Woman: That's a common problem. What did the incomplete ones leave out?
Man: Mostly the last section, the questions about income.
Woman: Then I wouldn't throw them away. You can still use their answers for the other sections. Just explain in your methods section why the numbers change from one table to the next.
Man: That makes sense. But it'll take me a few extra days to redo the analysis. Is there any chance of an extension?
Woman: I can give you until Tuesday, but no later, because I have to submit final grades the following week.

clips.context: You will hear part of a radio science program about temperatures in cities.
clips.script: Welcome back to Science Today. If you've ever noticed that the city feels hotter than the countryside on a summer evening, you're not imagining it. Scientists call this the urban heat island effect, and it can make a city center as much as seven degrees warmer than the surrounding area. The main reason is surprisingly simple. Dark surfaces, like asphalt roads and rooftops, absorb sunlight during the day and then release that heat slowly after the sun goes down. At the same time, cities have far fewer trees, and trees cool the air by releasing water through their leaves. So what can be done? Some cities have started painting rooftops white or light gray, which reflects much of the sunlight back into the sky. Others are planting trees along streets and turning empty lots into small parks. The results so far are encouraging. In one study, neighborhoods that added trees saw summer night temperatures drop by about two degrees. That may not sound like much, but for elderly residents, who are most at risk during heat waves, two degrees can make a real difference to their health. Researchers point out, however, that these solutions work best together. A single white roof won't change much on its own. It's the combination of many small changes across a whole neighborhood that really matters.

qs.q: According to the speaker, why are cities warmer than the countryside in the evening?
qs.ex: הקריין מסביר: ״Dark surfaces... absorb sunlight during the day and then release that heat slowly after the sun goes down״. העצים דווקא מקררים, והגגות הלבנים מחזירים את אור השמש.
o: City residents use more air conditioners at night.
Trees in cities release warm air through their leaves during the evening.
White rooftops trap sunlight inside buildings.
Dark surfaces release heat that they absorbed during the day.

qs.q: What point do researchers emphasize at the end of the segment?
qs.ex: בסוף נאמר: ״It's the combination of many small changes across a whole neighborhood that really matters״ – השילוב הוא העיקר, וגג לבן אחד לבדו לא ישנה הרבה.
o: White roofs are more effective than planting trees along city streets.
Two degrees is too small a change to affect health.
Many small changes together are more effective than any single one.
Only elderly residents benefit from cooler neighborhoods.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about the placebo effect.
clips.script: Today I want to talk about the placebo effect. A placebo is a treatment with no active ingredient, such as a sugar pill. You might expect it to do nothing, yet in many studies, a significant number of patients who receive a placebo report feeling better. For years, researchers assumed this was all in the patients' heads, that they were simply imagining the improvement. But more recent research suggests something more interesting. When people expect to feel better, their brains actually release natural pain-relieving chemicals. In other words, the improvement can be physically real. The effect also seems to depend on small details. Two pills work better than one, and expensive-looking pills work better than cheap ones. This is exactly why new drugs must be tested against a placebo. If a new medicine performs no better than a sugar pill, we can't say that the medicine itself is doing anything.

qs.q: According to more recent research, what causes the placebo effect?
qs.ex: המרצה אומר: ״When people expect to feel better, their brains actually release natural pain-relieving chemicals״. הרעיון שהכול ״בדמיון״ הוא ההסבר הישן שהמחקר החדש מערער.
o: Patients only imagine that they feel better.
Sugar pills contain small amounts of medicine.
Doctors give patients extra attention and care during medical studies.
Expectation leads the brain to release natural chemicals.

qs.q: Why does the lecturer mention expensive-looking pills?
qs.ex: הדוגמה באה אחרי המשפט ״The effect also seems to depend on small details״ – כדור שנראה יקר משפיע יותר, כלומר פרטים קטנים משנים את עוצמת האפקט.
o: To argue that new drugs are too expensive.
To explain why sugar pills are rarely used in medical research today.
To show that small details affect how strong the placebo effect is.
To show that patients prefer cheaper medicine.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between a student and his academic advisor.
clips.script:
Man: Thanks for meeting with me, Dr. Rivera. I need some help deciding what to do this summer.

The distance between the firm and the campus.
His low grades in engineering courses.
The difficulty of the summer courses.

Asking the firm to pay him for the internship.
Postponing graduation in order to gain more experience.
Doing the internship and taking the required courses online during the year.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about how babies learn language.
clips.script: Newborn babies are remarkable listeners. Research shows that at six months, infants can tell apart the sounds of almost any language in the world, including sounds that their own parents can't even hear. But by their first birthday, this ability narrows. Babies become experts in the sounds of the language around them and gradually lose their sensitivity to sounds they never hear. In a sense, they trade flexibility for efficiency.

qs.q: According to the lecturer, what happens to babies' listening ability by the age of one?
qs.ex: המרצה אומר: ״Babies become experts in the sounds of the language around them and gradually lose their sensitivity to sounds they never hear״ – היכולת מצטמצמת ומתמקדת בשפה הסביבתית.
o: It improves so that they can hear the sounds of every language in the world.
It disappears until they begin to speak.
It becomes focused on the sounds of the language around them.
It becomes weaker than their parents' ability.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between two students working on a group project.

o: A presentation that their professor has suddenly cancelled.
A group member who has not done his part of the work.
A grade they received on an earlier project.
A classmate who wants to join their group.

Ask for the presentation to be moved to next week.
Visit Daniel to check whether he is sick.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about an idea in economics.
clips.script: Let's turn to one of the most important ideas in economics: opportunity cost. Every time you make a choice, you give something up. The opportunity cost of a decision is the value of the best alternative that you didn't choose. Take a simple example. Suppose you decide to spend Saturday afternoon at the movies. The ticket costs twelve dollars, but that's not the full cost. If you could have spent those three hours at your part-time job, earning, say, forty-five dollars, then that lost income is also part of the real cost of the movie. Now, many people find this idea strange, because opportunity costs don't appear on any receipt. You never get a bill for the money you didn't earn. And that's exactly why people tend to ignore them. Studies show that consumers pay close attention to prices they can see and very little attention to hidden costs, such as time. Businesses and governments face the same problem on a larger scale. When a city spends money on a new stadium, the real question isn't only whether the stadium is useful. It's whether the same money could have done more good somewhere else, for example in schools or public transportation. Thinking in terms of opportunity cost won't tell you what to choose, but it forces you to compare your options honestly.

qs.q: In the movie example, what does the forty-five dollars represent?
qs.ex: המרצה אומר: ״that lost income is also part of the real cost of the movie״ – 45 הדולר הם ההכנסה שמוותרים עליה. מחיר הכרטיס הוא 12 דולר.
o: The total price of the movie ticket.
Income lost by going to the movies.
Money saved by not working on Saturday.
The cost of three movie tickets.

qs.q: According to the lecturer, why do people tend to ignore opportunity costs?
qs.ex: נאמר: ״opportunity costs don't appear on any receipt... And that's exactly why people tend to ignore them״ – אין עליהם חשבונית, ולכן לא שמים לב אליהם.
o: They are usually much smaller than real prices.
Governments do not allow them to be measured.
They only apply to large businesses.
They do not appear as an actual payment.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between a student and a librarian.
clips.script:
Man: Excuse me, I'm trying to read an article from this journal, but the website keeps asking me to pay.

He forgot the password to his student account.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about coral reefs.
clips.script: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support about a quarter of all marine species. Corals are actually animals, but they depend on tiny algae that live inside their tissues. The algae produce food through photosynthesis, and they also give coral its bright colors. When ocean water becomes too warm, even by just one or two degrees, this partnership breaks down. The stressed corals push the algae out, and without them, the corals turn white. This is called bleaching. A bleached coral isn't dead yet. If temperatures return to normal within a few weeks, the algae can come back and the coral can recover. But if the heat lasts too long, the coral starves. What worries scientists most is frequency. Bleaching events used to happen once every twenty-five years or so. Now, in some regions, they happen every few years, leaving reefs no time to recover.

qs.q: What causes corals to turn white?
qs.ex: נאמר: ״The stressed corals push the algae out, and without them, the corals turn white״. האלמוג המולבן עוד לא מת – ״A bleached coral isn't dead yet״.
o: They die as soon as the water warms by one degree.
They stop producing food through photosynthesis.
They are covered by sand from the ocean floor.
They lose the algae that live inside them.

qs.q: What worries scientists most?
qs.ex: המרצה אומר: ״What worries scientists most is frequency... leaving reefs no time to recover״ – התדירות הגבוהה לא משאירה לשוניות זמן להתאושש.
o: Bleaching now happens too often for reefs to recover.
Reefs cover too small a part of the ocean floor.
Algae are moving to colder parts of the ocean.
Scientists cannot predict when the next bleaching event will occur.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between a student and her thesis supervisor.
clips.script:
Woman: Professor Kim, I wanted to talk to you about my thesis topic. I'm thinking of changing it.
Man: Really? You've been working on social media and teenage friendships since September. What happened?
Woman: Nothing went wrong, exactly. It's just that I keep finding more studies that have already been published on the topic. I'm afraid I won't have anything new to say.
Man: I understand the feeling, but a lot of existing research isn't necessarily a bad sign. It means the topic matters, and it gives you a solid base to build on. The real question is whether you can find a gap.
Woman: A gap?
Man: Something those studies haven't looked at. For example, most of the research I know focuses on teenagers in big cities. Have you seen much about rural areas?
Woman: Actually, no. Almost every study I've read was done in a city.
Man: There you go. Teenagers in small towns might use social media very differently, maybe because their friends live farther apart. That could be a genuine contribution.
Woman: That's interesting. And my hometown is pretty rural, so I might even be able to find participants there.
Man: Exactly. So before you change direction completely, spend a week reading with that question in mind. Then come back and tell me whether it still feels like a dead end.

qs.q: Why does the student want to change her thesis topic?
qs.ex: היא אומרת: ״I keep finding more studies that have already been published on the topic. I'm afraid I won't have anything new to say״. היא גם מדגישה ש־״Nothing went wrong״, כך שלא מדובר בתוצאות מאכזבות.
o: Her research results were disappointing.
She has lost interest in social media.
She cannot find enough participants for her study in the city.
She thinks it has already been studied too much.

qs.q: What does the professor suggest?
qs.ex: הפרופסור מציע למצוא ״a gap... Something those studies haven't looked at״ – למשל בני נוער באזורים כפריים, נושא שהמחקר הקיים פספס.
o: Choosing a completely new topic within a week.
Focusing on an aspect that previous research has overlooked.
Repeating a well-known study in her hometown.
Reading only the studies that were done with teenagers in big cities.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about ancient building materials.
clips.script: Many Roman buildings have survived for two thousand years, while some modern concrete structures begin to crack after only fifty. For a long time, engineers couldn't explain the difference. Recent studies found that Roman concrete contained small pieces of lime. When water seeped into a crack, it reacted with the lime and formed new crystals, which sealed the crack. In effect, the concrete repaired itself.

qs.q: According to the lecturer, what made Roman concrete so long-lasting?
qs.ex: נאמר: ״When water seeped into a crack, it reacted with the lime and formed new crystals, which sealed the crack״ – הבטון ״תיקן את עצמו״. הוא כן נסדק, אבל הסדקים נאטמו.
o: It was protected from water by a layer of lime.
It could seal its own cracks when water got in.
It was made without any water at all.
It was harder than modern concrete and never cracked.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between a student and a writing center tutor.
clips.script:

Woman: Great, have a seat. What would you like to focus on today?

Man: I thought it would be more convincing to build up to it.

Man: So I should move my conclusion to the introduction?
Woman: More or less. State your claim clearly at the beginning, and then make sure each paragraph opens with a sentence that connects back to it.

qs.ex: המדריכה אומרת: ״your main claim doesn't appear until the last paragraph״. היא דווקא מציינת שיש בחיבור ״a lot of good facts״.
o: Its main argument appears only at the end.
It does not contain enough historical facts.
It is written like a mystery novel.
Its introduction is much too long.

qs.ex: ההמלצה: ״State your claim clearly at the beginning, and then make sure each paragraph opens with a sentence that connects back to it״. ״לבנות לאט״ היא בדיוק הגישה שהיא דוחה.
o: Stating the claim early and linking each paragraph to it.
Removing some of the facts from the essay.
Asking the professor to explain her comments on the essay in more detail.
Building up slowly to the main claim.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about a famous line of research in social psychology.
clips.script: In 1964, a New York newspaper reported that thirty-eight people had watched a crime from their windows and done nothing. Later investigations showed that the story was greatly exaggerated, but it inspired a famous line of research. Two psychologists, John Darley and Bibb Latané, wanted to know whether the presence of other people makes us less likely to help. In one experiment, students sat in separate rooms and talked to each other over an intercom. At some point, one participant, who was actually working with the researchers, seemed to have a medical emergency. When students believed they were the only other person listening, most of them quickly went for help. But when they believed four other people were also listening, only about a third did. The researchers called this the bystander effect. Their explanation was something they named diffusion of responsibility. When many people are present, each person feels less personally responsible and assumes that someone else will act. Now, here's the encouraging part. Later research found that the effect becomes much weaker when a situation is clearly dangerous, and also when people have learned about the bystander effect itself. So, in a way, just by sitting in this lecture today, you've made yourselves more likely to help.

qs.q: What did the intercom experiment show?
qs.ex: לבד – ״most of them quickly went for help״; כשחשבו שארבעה אחרים מאזינים – ״only about a third did״. כלומר נוכחות של אחרים מפחיתה את הנכונות לעזור.
o: Most people refused to help in any situation.
People helped more quickly when they believed other listeners were present.
People were less likely to help when they believed others were listening.
Students could not tell that the emergency was real.

qs.q: Why does the lecturer say the students are now more likely to help?
qs.ex: נאמר שהאפקט נחלש ״when people have learned about the bystander effect itself״, ולכן ״just by sitting in this lecture today, you've made yourselves more likely to help״.
o: They have experienced a real emergency.
Learning about the effect makes it weaker.
They are sitting together with many other people.
The newspaper story was shown to be exaggerated.

clips.script:

Woman: That's a relief. I was worried I'd have to learn every chapter by heart. Thanks.

qs.ex: הפרופסור אומר: ״you should understand the main ideas in them, but you don't need to memorize the details״. רוב השאלות יגיעו מההרצאות, לא מהקריאה.
o: Students should understand their main ideas.
They will not appear on the exam at all.
Most of the exam questions will be based on the readings.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about how astronomers find planets.
clips.script: How do astronomers find planets around other stars? These planets are far too small and dim to see directly, so scientists use indirect methods. The most successful one is called the transit method. When a planet passes in front of its star, as seen from Earth, it blocks a tiny portion of the star's light. A sensitive telescope can measure this drop in brightness, even when it's less than one percent. If the dip repeats at regular intervals, astronomers can conclude that a planet is orbiting the star, and the time between dips tells them how long one orbit takes. The size of the dip also reveals the planet's size, since a bigger planet blocks more light. The method has one important limitation, though. It only works if the planet's orbit is lined up with our view. Many planets are probably missed simply because they never pass between us and their star.

qs.q: What does the time between dips in brightness tell astronomers?
qs.ex: נאמר: ״the time between dips tells them how long one orbit takes״. את גודל כוכב הלכת מסיקים מגודל הירידה בבהירות, לא מהזמן שבין הירידות.
o: How long it takes the planet to complete one orbit.
How large the planet is.
How far the star is from Earth.
How bright the planet is when compared with the star it orbits.

qs.q: What limitation of the transit method does the lecturer mention?
qs.ex: המגבלה: ״It only works if the planet's orbit is lined up with our view״ – כוכבי לכת שלא עוברים בינינו לבין הכוכב מתפספסים. ירידות של פחות מאחוז דווקא כן נמדדות.
o: It can only find planets that are very large.
It requires telescopes that are not yet available.
It cannot measure any drop in a star's brightness of less than one percent.
It misses planets whose orbits do not pass between us and their star.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between two students about an assigned reading.
clips.script:
Man: Did you finish the reading for psychology? The one about taking notes?
Woman: Yes, and I found it really surprising. I always assumed typing notes was better, because you can write down so much more.

Woman: That sounds like a good compromise. Let me know how it goes.

Students who write by hand can record more information.
Handwritten notes are easier to read later.
Laptops distract students with the internet.

o: Stop using his laptop for taking notes in all of his classes.
Repeat the experiment described in the article.
Take handwritten notes in a course that focuses on ideas.
Use his laptop only for philosophy.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about octopuses.
clips.script: Octopuses are among the most intelligent invertebrates on Earth. They can open jars, escape from tanks, and even recognize individual human faces. What makes this so surprising is the way their nervous system is organized. About two-thirds of an octopus's neurons are located not in its brain, but in its arms. This means that each arm can, to some extent, react to its surroundings on its own.

o: Most of their neurons are located in their arms.
They have no brain at all.
They can recognize only other octopuses.
Their arms cannot move at all without signals from the brain.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between a student and a professor about an exam.

He did not show how he reached his answer.
He made a small mistake in his calculation.
He did not finish the question in time.

She will add them back if he explains his method to her now.
It is not possible, but the final exam is worth more.
He can receive partial credit for the correct answer.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about the history of medicine.
clips.script: In the 1840s, a Hungarian doctor named Ignaz Semmelweis was working at a large hospital in Vienna. The hospital had two maternity wards, and Semmelweis noticed something disturbing. In the first ward, which was run by doctors and medical students, about one in ten mothers died of fever after giving birth. In the second ward, run by midwives, the death rate was far lower. Semmelweis searched for an explanation, and he finally found it after a colleague died from an infection. The colleague had been cut by a student's knife while examining a dead body, and his symptoms were the same as the mothers'. Semmelweis realized that the doctors were going straight from examining dead bodies to delivering babies, carrying something deadly on their hands. The midwives, on the other hand, never examined dead bodies. He ordered all doctors to wash their hands in a chlorine solution, and the death rate dropped dramatically. You'd think he would have been celebrated. Instead, many doctors rejected his ideas. Some were offended by the suggestion that they were causing deaths. Others pointed out, quite fairly, that he couldn't explain why washing worked. Germ theory wouldn't be accepted for another twenty years. Semmelweis's story reminds us that in science, having the right answer isn't always enough.

qs.q: What led Semmelweis to his discovery?
qs.ex: ההסבר נמצא ״after a colleague died from an infection... his symptoms were the same as the mothers'״. תורת החיידקים התקבלה רק עשרים שנה מאוחר יותר.
o: A careful comparison of chlorine with several other cleaning products.
The death of a colleague who was injured while examining a body.
Complaints from the midwives in the second ward.
A theory about germs that he had read about.

qs.q: According to the lecturer, what was a reasonable objection to Semmelweis's ideas?
qs.ex: המרצה אומר: ״Others pointed out, quite fairly, that he couldn't explain why washing worked״ – המילה fairly מסמנת התנגדות סבירה. שיעור התמותה דווקא ירד ״dramatically״.
o: His results showed no real decrease in deaths.
He could not explain why handwashing was effective.
Chlorine was too dangerous to be used regularly in hospitals.
The midwives did not follow his instructions.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between a student and a teaching assistant.
clips.script:
Man: Hi. I missed the chemistry lab on Tuesday because I had the flu. Is there any way I can make it up?
Woman: Yes, but first you'll need a note from the health center confirming that you were sick. Once I have that, you can join the Thursday afternoon section instead of yours.
Man: Thursday works for me. Is there anything else I should do?
Woman: No, that's all.

qs.q: What does the teaching assistant require before the student can make up the lab?
qs.ex: העוזרת אומרת: ״first you'll need a note from the health center confirming that you were sick״, ובסוף מוסיפה ״that's all״ – אין דרישה נוספת.
o: Permission from the course professor.
An extra written assignment.
Online registration for the Thursday section.
A note confirming that he was ill.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about social networks.
clips.script: In the 1970s, a sociologist named Mark Granovetter asked a simple question: how do people actually find jobs? You might expect close friends and family to be the most helpful. But Granovetter found that most people heard about their jobs through acquaintances, people they knew only slightly, like former classmates or friends of friends. He called these connections weak ties. The reason they're so valuable is that your close friends usually know the same people and hear the same news that you do. Acquaintances, on the other hand, move in different circles, so they have access to information you would never hear otherwise. Granovetter described this idea in an article with a memorable title, The Strength of Weak Ties. Today, the same idea helps explain why professional networking websites can be so useful: they keep us connected to hundreds of people we rarely see.

qs.q: According to Granovetter's findings, how did most people find their jobs?
qs.ex: נאמר: ״most people heard about their jobs through acquaintances, people they knew only slightly״. חברים קרובים ומשפחה הם מה ש״היינו מצפים״, אבל זה לא מה שנמצא.
o: Through close friends and family members.
Through advertisements in newspapers.
Through people they knew only slightly.
Through professional networking websites.

qs.q: Why, according to the lecturer, are weak ties valuable?
qs.ex: המרצה מסביר: ״Acquaintances... move in different circles, so they have access to information you would never hear otherwise״. דווקא החברים הקרובים ״know the same people״.
o: They are more loyal than close friends.
They are much easier to maintain than close, long-term friendships.
They provide information from outside one's usual social circle.
They usually know the same people that we do.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between a student and a professor about a research position.
clips.script:
Woman: Dr. Patel, I saw your notice about a research assistant position in your lab. I'd love to apply.
Man: Wonderful. Tell me a little about yourself. What year are you in?
Woman: I'm a second-year biology student. I took your genetics course last semester.
Man: Oh yes, I remember. You wrote that excellent paper on fruit flies. So what interests you about the position?
Woman: Mainly, I want to see what real research looks like. In class, every experiment works perfectly. I'm curious about what happens when it doesn't.
Man: Well, you'll see plenty of that. I should warn you, though. The first few months aren't very exciting. You'd be cleaning equipment, preparing samples, and entering data. It's only later that assistants start designing their own small experiments.
Woman: That's fine with me. I know I have to learn the basics first.
Man: Good attitude. The other thing is time. I need someone for at least ten hours a week, including some early mornings, because the samples have to be checked before eight.
Woman: My classes all start after ten, so mornings are actually easier for me than afternoons.
Man: Then it sounds like a good fit. Send me your transcript and a short statement about your interests, and I'll make a decision by the end of next week.

qs.q: Why does the student want the position?
qs.ex: היא אומרת: ״I want to see what real research looks like. In class, every experiment works perfectly. I'm curious about what happens when it doesn't״.
o: To earn money for her tuition.
To design her own experiments immediately.
To experience real research, including experiments that fail.
To improve her final grade in the genetics course she took last semester.

qs.q: What does the professor warn the student about?
qs.ex: הפרופסור מזהיר: ״The first few months aren't very exciting. You'd be cleaning equipment, preparing samples, and entering data״ – עבודה שגרתית. הבקרים דווקא נוחים לה.
o: Her schedule does not allow her to work mornings.
Assistants are not allowed to handle samples.
Only students in their final year are accepted.
The work in the first months is mostly routine.

clips.context: You will hear part of a radio report about birds and cities.
clips.script: Every year, millions of migrating birds die after flying into tall buildings. Most of these birds migrate at night and use the stars to find their way. Bright city lights confuse them, drawing them toward buildings and away from their natural routes. Some cities have found a simple solution. During migration season, office buildings turn off unnecessary lights after midnight. In some places, bird deaths have dropped by more than half.

qs.q: What solution does the speaker describe?
qs.ex: נאמר: ״During migration season, office buildings turn off unnecessary lights after midnight״, ובעקבות זאת מקרי המוות ירדו ביותר מחצי.
o: Building shorter office towers in city centers.
Using brighter lights to guide the birds safely around tall buildings.
Turning off building lights at night during migration season.
Changing the routes that birds use to migrate.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between a student and a study abroad advisor.
clips.script:
Woman: So you're interested in studying abroad next spring?
Man: Yes, I'd like to go to Spain. My Spanish is pretty good, and I think living there would really improve it. But I'm worried about falling behind in my major.
Woman: That's a common concern. What's your major again?
Man: Economics.
Woman: Then you're in luck. Our partner university in Madrid offers several economics courses, and most of them have already been approved for credit here. As long as you choose from the approved list, you won't lose any time.
Man: Really? That's great. Are the courses taught in Spanish?
Woman: Some are, and some are in English. You can choose. But since you want to improve your Spanish, I'd suggest taking at least one in Spanish.
Man: That makes sense. What's the next step?
Woman: The application deadline is October fifteenth, and you'll need two recommendation letters, so I'd ask your professors soon.

qs.q: Why is the student worried?
qs.ex: הוא אומר: ״I'm worried about falling behind in my major״. על הספרדית שלו הוא אומר ״pretty good״.
o: He does not speak Spanish well enough.
He thinks studying abroad might slow his progress in his major.
He has missed the application deadline.
His professors have refused to write him the recommendation letters he needs.

qs.q: What does the advisor tell him about the economics courses in Madrid?
qs.ex: היועצת אומרת: ״most of them have already been approved for credit here״. היא גם מציינת שחלק מהקורסים באנגלית, כך שלא כולם בספרדית.
o: They are all taught in Spanish.
They are more difficult than the courses at home.
They must be approved by his professors at home after he returns from Spain.
Most of them are already approved for credit at his university.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about language and thought.
clips.script: Here's a question. If I asked you where your left hand is, you'd simply raise it. But imagine speaking a language that has no words for left and right at all. That's the case in Guugu Yimithirr, a language spoken by a small community in northern Australia. Instead of left and right, speakers use the compass directions: north, south, east, and west. They don't say the cup is to your left. They say the cup is to your north. Even a sentence like there's an ant on your southern leg is completely normal. What fascinates researchers is what this does to the mind. To speak this way, you have to know which direction you're facing at every moment. And speakers do. In experiments, they could point accurately to the north even inside a building with no windows, something most English speakers find very difficult. This has been used as evidence for a famous and controversial idea, that the language we speak shapes the way we think. Now, I want to be careful here. It's possible that the environment shaped both the language and the skill, rather than the language causing the skill. As always, correlation isn't causation. But at the very least, these speakers show us that something we consider basic, like left and right, isn't universal.

qs.q: What is unusual about Guugu Yimithirr?
qs.ex: המרצה אומר: ״Instead of left and right, speakers use the compass directions: north, south, east, and west״.
o: It describes location using compass directions instead of left and right.
It has many more words for left and right than English or other languages do.
It is spoken only inside buildings with no windows.
It has no words for the directions north and south.

qs.q: What caution does the lecturer express?
qs.ex: הוא מזהיר: ״It's possible that the environment shaped both the language and the skill, rather than the language causing the skill״ – מתאם אינו סיבתיות.
o: The experiments were done with too few speakers to support any conclusion.
The speakers' skill might not be caused by their language.
English speakers can also point north easily.
The language may soon disappear completely.

clips.context: You will hear a conversation between two classmates.
clips.script:
Woman: You weren't in class this morning. Professor Walsh changed the due date for the lab report.
Man: Oh no. Is it earlier now?
Woman: No, it's later, next Monday instead of Friday. She said a lot of people had trouble with the new software, so she wanted to give everyone more time.
Man: That's great news. I was nowhere near finished.

qs.q: Why did the professor change the due date?
qs.ex: נאמר: ״a lot of people had trouble with the new software, so she wanted to give everyone more time״. המועד נדחה ליום שני – לא הוקדם.
o: Many students had difficulties with the software.
The man had missed several classes.
The professor will be away on Friday.
The lab report was made longer.

clips.context: You will hear part of a lecture about art history.
clips.script: We often think of artistic movements as the result of new ideas. But sometimes technology plays a surprising role. Take Impressionism. Before the 1840s, painters usually had to mix their own paints from powder and oil, and the paint was difficult to store and carry, so most of them worked indoors, in their studios. Then, in 1841, an American painter invented the metal paint tube. Suddenly, artists could carry ready-made paint wherever they went. This made it much easier to paint outdoors, directly in front of their subject. And that's exactly what the Impressionists did. Painters like Monet set up their easels in fields and along rivers, trying to capture the changing light at a particular moment. The painter Renoir supposedly said that without paint in tubes, there would have been no Impressionism. Whether or not he really said it, the point stands: a simple invention helped change the direction of art.

qs.q: According to the lecturer, how did the paint tube affect artists?
qs.ex: נאמר: ״artists could carry ready-made paint wherever they went. This made it much easier to paint outdoors״.
o: It allowed them to mix new colors in the studio.
It made it practical to paint outdoors.
It made paint much cheaper to buy.
It encouraged them to paint indoor scenes.

qs.q: Why does the lecturer mention Renoir?
qs.ex: הציטוט ״without paint in tubes, there would have been no Impressionism״ תומך בטענה שהמצאה טכנולוגית השפיעה על התנועה. המרצה עצמו מסייג: ״Whether or not he really said it״.
o: To show that Renoir invented the paint tube.
To support the claim that technology influenced Impressionism.
To argue that Renoir disliked painting outdoors.
To prove that the famous quotation by Renoir is definitely accurate.

clips.context: You will hear part of a radio interview with a biologist.
clips.script:
Host: My guest today is Dr. Laura Chen, a biologist who studies one of our most common behaviors: yawning. Dr. Chen, why do we yawn?
Guest: Well, the honest answer is that we're still not completely sure. For a long time, people believed we yawn because we need more oxygen. But when researchers gave people extra oxygen to breathe, they yawned just as often. So that explanation doesn't really hold up.
Host: So what's the leading theory now?
Guest: One popular idea is that yawning cools the brain. When you yawn, you take in a large amount of air, and stretching the jaw increases blood flow to the head. Some studies found that people yawn more often when the air is cooler than their body, and less often when it's very hot outside.
Host: Interesting. And what about the fact that yawning is contagious? I've probably yawned twice just talking about it.
Guest: You're not alone. Contagious yawning seems to be linked to empathy, our ability to connect with other people. People are more likely to catch a yawn from a family member than from a stranger. And young children usually don't catch yawns until they're about four or five, which is roughly when they start to understand other people's feelings.
Host: So yawning might be a social behavior as well as a physical one.
Guest: Exactly, and that's what makes it such an interesting thing to study.

qs.q: Why was the oxygen theory of yawning rejected?
qs.ex: החוקרת מסבירה: ״when researchers gave people extra oxygen to breathe, they yawned just as often״ – ולכן ההסבר של חוסר חמצן לא מחזיק.
o: People yawned less often in cool air.
Yawning was shown to increase blood flow to the head.
Children do not yawn until the age of four.
Extra oxygen did not reduce how often people yawned.

qs.q: What evidence links contagious yawning to empathy?
qs.ex: נאמר: ״People are more likely to catch a yawn from a family member than from a stranger״, וגם שילדים מתחילים ״להידבק״ בפיהוק בגיל שבו הם מבינים רגשות של אחרים.
o: People catch yawns more easily from those they are close to.
People yawn more often in cool weather.
Strangers are more likely to make people yawn.
Yawning cools the brain during conversations.

cont.script: Many people believe that multitasking makes them more productive. They answer emails during meetings and check their phones while studying. However, research tells a different story. When we switch between tasks, our brains need time to refocus, and these small delays quickly add up. As a result, people who multitask regularly
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: complete their tasks faster than people who focus on one thing.
should always turn off their phones before going to sleep.
often take longer to finish their work and make more mistakes.
were first studied by scientists in the nineteenth century.
cont.ex: המילה However מסמנת שהמחקר סותר את האמונה, ו־״these small delays quickly add up״ מוביל לתוצאה שלילית: עבודה איטית יותר וטעויות רבות יותר.

cont.script: Honeybees have a remarkable way of sharing information. When a worker bee discovers a good patch of flowers, she returns to the hive and performs what scientists call a waggle dance. The other bees watch closely. The direction of the dance tells them which way to fly, while the length of the dance
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: tells them how far away the flowers are.
explains why bees cannot see the color red.
keeps the hive warm during the winter months.
shows that bees prefer to collect food alone.
cont.ex: המבנה ״The direction... tells them which way to fly, while the length...״ מחייב מידע נוסף על מיקום הפרחים – המרחק. שאר האפשרויות לא עוסקות בהעברת מידע על הפרחים.

cont.script: When the university library first opened in 1920, it held only a few thousand books, and students had to ask a librarian to bring each one from a closed room. Over the following decades, the collection grew enormously. Today, however, the most important change is not the number of books, but
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: the number of books, which has grown enormously.
the librarian who once had to bring every book from a closed room.
the year in which the library first opened.
the fact that most resources can now be reached online.
cont.ex: המבנה ״not the number of books, but...״ דורש שינוי מסוג אחר. האפשרות על מספר הספרים סותרת את ה־not, והאחרות מתייחסות לעבר ולא לשינוי של היום.

cont.script: Procrastination is often described as a problem of laziness or poor time management. But psychologists who study it have reached a different conclusion. They argue that people usually delay tasks because those tasks make them feel anxious, bored, or unsure of themselves. In other words, procrastination is less about time and more about
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: having too much free time during the week.
avoiding unpleasant feelings.
finding a better calendar or planning app.
the laziness that some people are born with.
cont.ex: ״In other words״ מסכם את מה שנאמר: אנשים דוחים משימות שגורמות להם ״feel anxious, bored, or unsure״ – כלומר מדובר ברגשות. העצלות היא בדיוק ההסבר שהפסיכולוגים דוחים.

cont.script: In 1815, Mount Tambora in Indonesia erupted, sending enormous amounts of ash and gas high into the atmosphere. Over the following months, these particles spread around the globe and blocked part of the sunlight. As a result, the following year became known in Europe and North America as the year without a summer, because
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: temperatures reached record highs in July.
snow fell in June and crops failed in many areas.
the eruption was never recorded by scientists.
Indonesia is located very close to the equator.
cont.ex: החלקיקים ״blocked part of the sunlight״, ולכן הקיץ היה קר במיוחד – שלג ביוני ויבולים שנכשלו. טמפרטורות שיא סותרות את ״year without a summer״.

cont.script: Good morning, everyone. Last week we discussed how plants produce energy through photosynthesis. Today I'd like to look at the other side of the process. Plants don't only produce energy; just like animals, they also need to use it in order to grow. So the main question for today's lecture is
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: how sunlight was first measured by early scientists in the laboratory.
how plants break down the sugars that they have produced.
which kinds of animals eat the most plants.
why we will not discuss plants this semester.
cont.ex: המרצה מכריז על ״the other side of the process״ – איך צמחים משתמשים באנרגיה. פירוק הסוכרים שייצרו הוא בדיוק השימוש באנרגיה הזאת.

cont.script: Since remote work became common, many companies have reported that their employees are just as productive at home as in the office. Yet some managers remain unconvinced. Their main concern is not productivity itself, but something that is much harder to measure. They worry that without daily face-to-face contact, employees
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: will find it harder to build relationships and share ideas informally.
will finish their daily tasks much more slowly than they did in the office.
have always preferred to work in large open offices.
can measure their own productivity more accurately.
cont.ex: הדאגה ״is not productivity itself, but something... harder to measure״, ולכן האפשרות על עבודה איטית יותר (פרודוקטיביות) נפסלת. קשרים ורעיונות לא פורמליים הם בדיוק דבר שקשה למדוד.

cont.script: Antibiotics are among the greatest medical discoveries of the twentieth century. They have saved millions of lives by killing harmful bacteria. However, every time antibiotics are used, a few bacteria may survive because of small genetic differences. These survivors then multiply and pass on their genes, and over time,
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: they can form whole populations that the drugs no longer affect.
antibiotics become stronger and more effective against these bacteria.
doctors discovered penicillin by accident.
the bacteria lose their ability to reproduce.
cont.ex: החיידקים ששרדו ״multiply and pass on their genes״ – ולכן נוצרת אוכלוסייה עמידה. המילה However כבר רמזה על בעיה, לא על שיפור בתרופות.

cont.script: It is often said that adults cannot learn a new language as well as children. There is some truth in this, especially when it comes to pronunciation. But in other areas, adults actually have an advantage. Because they already understand how grammar works in their own language, they
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: usually develop a perfect accent within a few weeks.
should avoid learning more than one language at a time.
can often learn new grammatical rules faster than young children.
often forget the grammar of their first language while learning a second one.
cont.ex: הדובר מבטיח ״adults actually have an advantage״ ומקשר אותו להבנת דקדוק. מבטא מושלם סותר את מה שנאמר על הגייה.

cont.script: Cacti are perfectly adapted to life in the desert. Instead of wide, flat leaves, which would lose a lot of water, they have sharp spines. Their thick stems can store water for months. And unlike most plants, which open their pores during the day, cacti open them only at night, when
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: the sun is at its strongest and hottest.
the cooler air means that less water escapes.
their spines fall off and slowly grow back.
they stop storing water in their stems.
cont.ex: כל הקטע עוסק בחיסכון במים, ולכן פתיחת הנקבוביות בלילה מוסברת באוויר הקריר שבו פחות מים מתאדים. בלילה השמש לא ״at its strongest״.

cont.script: In recent years, scientists have tried to repeat many well-known psychology experiments. Surprisingly, a large number of them failed to produce the same results the second time. This has become known as the replication crisis. Some researchers see it as a disaster for the field, but others argue that it is actually
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: proof that psychology experiments are always reliable.
a disaster that will destroy the entire field.
a sign that science is correcting its own mistakes.
the reason that scientists stopped doing experiments.
cont.ex: המבנה ״Some... see it as a disaster, but others argue that it is actually...״ דורש עמדה חיובית מנוגדת. ״אסון״ חוזר על העמדה הראשונה, ו״ניסויים תמיד אמינים״ סותר את העובדות.

cont.script: Many parents complain that their teenage children stay up late at night and are almost impossible to wake in the morning. It's easy to blame phones or video games. But biologists point out that during adolescence, the body's internal clock actually shifts. Teenagers naturally start to feel sleepy about two hours later than adults, which is why some schools
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: require teenagers to go to bed at eight o'clock.
have decided to start classes later in the morning.
have moved important exams to the earliest hour of the day.
no longer allow students to play video games.
cont.ex: ״which is why״ מחייב תוצאה הגיונית מהשעון הביולוגי המאוחר: התחלת לימודים מאוחרת יותר. איסור משחקים מתאים להסבר שהביולוגים דוחים.

cont.script: Coffee is one of the most popular drinks in the world, but its origins are surprisingly uncertain. According to a popular legend, it was discovered in Ethiopia by a goat herder who noticed that his goats became unusually energetic after eating certain red berries. Historians, however, point out that
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: goats are known to dislike the taste of berries.
no written record of this story appears until centuries later.
coffee is now grown in many countries around the world.
the goat herder later opened the first café in Europe to sell the drink.
cont.ex: ״Historians, however״ מציג הסתייגות מהאגדה, בהתאם ל־״origins are surprisingly uncertain״. העובדה שאין תיעוד כתוב עד מאות שנים אחר כך מטילה ספק בסיפור.

cont.script: For most of the twentieth century, cities were designed around the car. Wide roads and large parking lots took up a huge amount of space. In recent years, however, a number of cities have begun to rethink this approach. Paris, for example, has removed tens of thousands of parking spaces and
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: replaced many of them with bicycle lanes and green areas.
built several new highways through the city center.
encouraged more residents to drive to work every day.
was designed by a famous architect in the 1800s.
cont.ex: ״rethink this approach״ פירושו התרחקות מתכנון סביב הרכב. שבילי אופניים ושטחים ירוקים מתאימים לכך, וכבישים מהירים חדשים הם ההפך.

cont.script: Most students prepare for exams by rereading their notes and textbooks. It feels productive, because the material seems more familiar each time. But studies on memory suggest that a far more effective strategy is to test yourself. When you try to recall information without looking at it, your brain
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: forgets the material more quickly than it would after rereading the notes.
prefers to read the same page several times.
strengthens the connections you will need to remember it later.
needs much more sleep than usual.
cont.ex: הדובר טוען שבחינה עצמית היא ״far more effective״, ולכן ההמשך צריך להסביר למה היא עוזרת לזיכרון – חיזוק הקשרים במוח.

cont.script: It is often said that we know more about the surface of the Moon than about the bottom of our own oceans. This may sound like an exaggeration, but it's largely true. Only a small part of the ocean floor has been mapped in detail. The main reason for this is that
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: the Moon is much closer to us than the ocean floor.
the ocean floor is completely flat and has no interesting features to map.
the surface of the Moon is covered with water.
water blocks the radar signals that satellites use to map land.
cont.ex: ״The main reason״ מחייב הסבר למה קשה למפות את קרקעית הים. המים חוסמים את אותות המכ״ם של הלוויינים. הירח אינו קרוב יותר מקרקעית הים.

cont.script: Thank you all for coming. Today's workshop is about negotiation. Many people think that negotiation is only for business deals or salary discussions. But in fact, we negotiate all the time: with roommates over chores, with friends over weekend plans, even with ourselves. So the first thing I'd like you to do is
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?

cont.script: Many people assume that when they put plastic in the recycling bin, it will be turned into something new. Unfortunately, the reality is more complicated. Only certain types of plastic can be recycled easily, and even those can be recycled only a limited number of times, because

it can be recycled forever without losing quality.

cont.script: The tides that rise and fall along our coasts are caused mainly by the Moon. cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?

cont.script: Researchers once believed that raising children with two languages would confuse them and slow down their development. Today, this view has largely been abandoned. cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?

prevent children from learning to read.

train the brain to control attention more effectively.

cont.script: Before we start the review session, I want to say something about the final exam. cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?

don't worry too much about what each question asks.
read each question twice before you start writing.
write your answers as fast as you can.

o: immediately recognized that it was white wine.
refused to taste a wine that was red.
said that it tasted exactly like water.
described it with words normally used for red wine.

cont.script: Apps that connect drivers and delivery workers with customers have created millions of flexible jobs. Supporters say these jobs allow people to choose when and how much they work. Critics, on the other hand, point out a serious drawback. Because these workers are usually not considered employees, they
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: can choose exactly when, where, and how much they want to work each week.
are required to work every day in a central office.
often do not receive benefits such as health insurance or paid vacation.
usually earn more than the managers of the company.

cont.script: For centuries, it was widely believed that the Egyptian pyramids were built by slaves. In the 1990s, however, archaeologists discovered the tombs of workers buried close to the pyramids. cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?

the pyramids were built in the 1990s.
bread was not eaten in ancient Egypt.
they were respected workers rather than slaves.

cont.script: Crows are often seen as pests, but they are also among the most intelligent animals on Earth. In laboratory experiments, crows have solved puzzles that require several steps, such as using one tool to get another tool. Perhaps most impressively, some wild crows in Japan have learned to

forget where their own nests are located.
avoid human cities completely.
live underwater for several weeks.

cont.script: The effect of raising the minimum wage is one of the most debated questions in economics. Traditional theory predicts that if workers become more expensive, employers will hire fewer of them. Yet when economists studied real cases in which the minimum wage was raised, several studies found

that economists had never studied this question.
that the minimum wage had not actually been raised.
little or no drop in employment.

cont.script: Ask people why it's hotter in summer than in winter, and many will say it's because Earth is closer to the Sun in summer. It's a reasonable guess, but it's wrong. In fact, Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, during winter in the Northern Hemisphere. The real cause of the seasons is
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?

the distance between Earth and the Sun.
the amount of cloud in the sky.
the speed at which the Moon travels.

cont.script: Many students like to listen to music while they study, and some claim it helps them concentrate. Research on this question has produced mixed results. Instrumental music, without lyrics, seems to cause few problems for most people. Songs with words, however, can be quite distracting, especially when
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: the student is not doing anything at all.
the music is played without any lyrics.
the task involves reading or writing.
the student has already finished studying.
cont.ex: מילים בשיר מתחרות עם מילים במשימה, ולכן ההפרעה גדולה במיוחד בקריאה ובכתיבה. מוזיקה ״without any lyrics״ סותרת את ״Songs with words״.

cont.script: Welcome to the Museum of Natural History. Before we begin our tour, I'd like to give you a few quick reminders. Please keep your bags with you at all times, and stay with the group as we move between galleries. Photography is allowed in most rooms, but please don't use a flash, because
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: the museum closes at six o'clock this evening.
photography is not allowed anywhere in the building.
the tour will finish in the gift shop.
strong light can damage some of the older objects.

cont.script: Sharks have a frightening reputation, largely because of films that show them as hunters of humans. In reality, shark attacks are extremely rare. You are statistically more likely to be struck by lightning than to be bitten by a shark. In fact, humans pose a much greater threat to sharks, since
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: sharks attack thousands of swimmers along popular beaches every summer.
lightning rarely strikes the open ocean.
millions of them are caught by fishing boats every year.
most films about sharks are made in Hollywood.

cont.script: When city officials first proposed turning empty lots into community gardens, many residents were doubtful. They expected the gardens to be abandoned within a year. Five years later, the program has been a surprising success. Not only do the gardens produce fresh vegetables for local families, but they have also
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: been abandoned by almost all of the residents.
made vegetables much more expensive in the local shops and markets.
been turned back into empty lots.
brought together neighbors who had never spoken before.

cont.script: In 1610, Galileo pointed his telescope at Jupiter and noticed four small points of light near the planet. Night after night, their positions changed. everything in the sky revolves around Earth.
telescopes had not yet been invented.

cont.script: In a famous study, shoppers in a supermarket were offered free samples of jam. On some days, the table displayed twenty-four different flavors; on other days, only six. unable to choose a flavor to taste.

attracted to the table in greater numbers.

cont.script: When people talk about melting ice and rising sea levels, they often imagine the ice floating in the Arctic Ocean. But melting sea ice actually has very little effect on sea level, just as melting ice cubes don't make a glass of water overflow. The real concern is ice on land, such as
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?
o: the ice cubes in a glass of water.
the huge ice sheets that cover Greenland and Antarctica.
the floating ice that covers large parts of the Arctic Ocean.
the rain that falls over tropical forests.

cont.script: We all know that exercise is good for the heart and the muscles. But scientists are discovering that it may be just as important for the brain. In one study with older adults, those who walked regularly for a year showed growth in the hippocampus, a part of the brain that
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?

cont.script: Twice a year, many countries change their clocks by one hour. The idea, which became popular during the First World War, was to save energy by making better use of daylight in the evening. Today, though, many experts question whether the practice still makes sense, pointing out that
cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?

people enjoy longer and brighter summer evenings.
it was designed to make better use of daylight.
the energy it saves today is very small.

cont.q: Which of the following is the most suitable continuation?

found only in China.

This suggests that the main cause is

people themselves, who are drawn to surprising stories.

wr.prompt: Many universities now offer degree programs that are taught entirely online. Some people believe that online degrees are just as valuable as traditional ones, while others disagree. Write a response in which you state your opinion and support it with reasons and examples.
tips: הכריעו כבר במשפט הראשון: האם תואר מקוון שווה ערך לתואר רגיל? עמדה ברורה עדיפה על ״יש יתרונות וחסרונות״.
בחרו שתי סיבות שונות, למשל גמישות ונגישות מול חוסר באינטראקציה אישית, ולכל אחת תנו דוגמה קונקרטית (סטודנט עובד, מעבדה במדעים).
הזכירו בקצרה את הצד השני ודחו אותו (While some argue that..., ...), וסיימו במשפט מסכם שחוזר לעמדה.
wr.model: In my opinion, an online degree can be just as valuable as a traditional one, as long as the program is demanding. First, online programs make higher education available to people who could not otherwise study. For example, a nurse who works night shifts can complete a degree in management without leaving her job. Second, online courses often require more independent work, and this develops skills that employers value, such as time management and self-discipline. While some argue that online students miss out on face-to-face discussion, many programs now include live video seminars and group projects. Admittedly, fields that depend on laboratory work, like chemistry, are harder to teach online. However, for most subjects, the quality of the teaching matters more than the place where it happens. Therefore, employers should judge graduates by their knowledge, not by how they studied.

wr.prompt: Some universities require all students to take courses outside their major, such as a science student taking a literature course. Others allow students to focus only on their main subject. Which approach do you think is better? Write a response in which you state your opinion and support it with reasons and examples.
tips: השאלה דורשת בחירה בין שתי גישות. כתבו במפורש איזו מהן עדיפה בעיניכם, ואל תתארו את שתיהן בלי להכריע.
השתמשו בדוגמה מוחשית מהפרומפט או דומה לה: סטודנט למדעי המחשב שלומד אתיקה, או סטודנטית לספרות שלומדת סטטיסטיקה.
גוונו במילות קישור (Furthermore, As a result, On the other hand) והקפידו לא לחרוג מ־150 מילים.
wr.model: I believe universities should require students to take some courses outside their major. To begin with, many modern problems cannot be solved with knowledge from a single field. A computer science student who takes a course in ethics, for instance, will be better prepared to think about how artificial intelligence affects people's privacy. Furthermore, these courses help students discover new interests. A friend of mine took an economics course only because it was required, and she eventually changed her major. On the other hand, critics claim that such courses waste time and money. This is a fair concern, so the requirement should be limited to two or three courses. In this way, students still gain deep knowledge in their own field. Overall, a small number of required courses outside the major produces graduates who are both specialists and broad thinkers.

wr.prompt: Some educators argue that elementary school students should not be given homework, because children need time to play and rest after school. Others believe homework is essential for learning. Write a response in which you state your opinion and support it with reasons and examples.
tips: אפשר לנקוט עמדת ביניים (למשל: מעט שיעורי בית, קצרים), אבל נסחו אותה כעמדה ברורה אחת ולא כהתלבטות.
חשבו על נימוקים משני הצדדים: הרגלי למידה ותרגול מול עייפות, משחק וזמן משפחה. בחרו את החזקים ביותר לעמדה שלכם.
משפט פתיחה טוב חוזר על השאלה במילים שלכם; אל תעתיקו את הפרומפט מילה במילה.
wr.model: In my view, young children should receive some homework, but only a small amount. On the one hand, short daily tasks help children build good habits. A child who spends fifteen minutes reading every evening learns to work independently, and this skill will be essential in high school. Homework also shows parents what their children are learning, so they can offer help when it is needed. On the other hand, long assignments can do more harm than good. After six hours at school, children need time to play outside, see friends and rest. Research suggests that at this age, large amounts of homework do little to improve grades and may make children dislike learning. Therefore, the best solution is a balance: brief, meaningful tasks such as reading or practicing multiplication, rather than hours of worksheets. In this way, children can learn responsibility and still enjoy their childhood.

wr.prompt: Some people prefer to work on projects as part of a team, while others prefer to work alone. Which do you think leads to better results? Write a response in which you state your opinion and support it with reasons and examples.
tips: שאלה של העדפה אישית מזמינה דוגמה מהניסיון שלכם – פרויקט בצבא, בעבודה או בבית הספר – וזה מצוין, כל עוד הדוגמה קצרה.
הסבירו למה הדוגמה מוכיחה את הטענה; אל תסתפקו בסיפור.
סיימו במשפט מסכם שמשיב ישירות לשאלה ״which leads to better results״.
wr.model: Although working alone has some advantages, I believe that teamwork usually leads to better results. The main reason is that a team combines different skills and points of view. When I prepared a presentation with three classmates last year, one of us was excellent at research, another at design, and I was responsible for writing. None of us could have produced such a strong result alone. In addition, team members can spot each other's mistakes. A single person may not notice a weakness in an argument, but a colleague often will. It is true that teamwork can be slow, especially when members disagree or when one person does not contribute. However, these problems can be reduced by dividing tasks clearly and setting deadlines. For these reasons, I am convinced that a well-organized team will almost always achieve more than an individual working alone.

wr.prompt: Governments spend billions of dollars every year on space exploration. Some people believe this money should instead be used to solve problems on Earth, such as poverty and disease. Write a response in which you state your opinion and support it with reasons and examples.
tips: זהו נושא ״גדול״ – הימנעו מהכללות ריקות. דוגמה ספציפית (לוויינים לחיזוי מזג אוויר, טכנולוגיות שפותחו בחלל) חזקה יותר מסיסמה.
התייחסו לטיעון הנגד המרכזי (עוני ומחלות) והראו למה הוא לא מבטל את עמדתכם, או למה הוא מכריע.
שימו לב לזמנים: 12 דקות זה מעט. השאירו דקה וחצי לבדיקת שגיאות ולמונה המילים.
wr.model: I believe that governments should continue to invest in space exploration, even though problems on Earth are urgent. First, space research often leads to technology that improves daily life. Satellites, for example, allow scientists to predict storms and droughts, which helps farmers and saves lives. Similarly, many medical devices were first developed for astronauts. Second, the amount of money spent on space is actually small compared with national budgets for health or defense. Cancelling space programs would not end poverty. Of course, it would be wrong to ignore hunger and disease while sending rockets to Mars. Nevertheless, the two goals do not have to compete. A society can fund hospitals and also support research that expands human knowledge. In conclusion, space exploration is not a luxury but an investment that brings practical benefits back to Earth.

wr.prompt: Some cities have made public transportation, such as buses and trains, completely free for everyone. Supporters say this reduces traffic and pollution, while critics say it is too expensive. Write a response in which you state your opinion and support it with reasons and examples.
tips: הפרומפט כבר נותן טיעון לכל צד. אל תחזרו עליהם כמות שהם – פתחו אותם עם הסבר ודוגמה משלכם.
אוצר מילים שימושי: reduce traffic, air pollution, funding, taxpayers, low-income residents.
אם אתם בעד – הציעו בקצרה מאיפה יגיע הכסף; זה הופך את הטיעון לבוגר ומשכנע.
wr.model: In my opinion, making public transportation free is a smart policy, despite its cost. The most important benefit is environmental. If buses and trains cost nothing, many people will leave their cars at home, which means less traffic and cleaner air. In crowded cities, this could also save commuters hours every week. Another advantage is fairness. Low-income residents spend a large share of their salaries on travel, and free transportation would give them better access to jobs and education. Critics are right that someone has to pay for the service. However, cities already spend huge sums on building roads and treating pollution-related illnesses. Part of this money, together with a small tax on parking, could fund free transportation. In short, although the policy is expensive, its benefits for the environment and for society make it worth the price.

wr.prompt: Many students take a gap year between high school and university in order to work, travel, or volunteer. Some people think this is a valuable experience, while others think it delays students' education and careers. Write a response in which you state your opinion and support it with reasons and examples.
tips: בישראל אפשר להיעזר בדוגמה מוכרת: השירות הצבאי או הטיול שאחריו כ״שנת פער״ שמשפיעה על הבגרות.
שימו לב למילים delay ו־valuable בפרומפט – אפשר להשתמש במילים נרדפות (postpone, worthwhile) כדי להראות עושר לשוני.
בנו כל פסקה סביב רעיון אחד ומשפט פתיחה ברור; חיבור של 130 מילים יכול להיות פסקה אחת מאורגנת היטב.
wr.model: I strongly believe that a gap year is a worthwhile experience for most students. To begin with, it gives young people time to discover what they really want to study. Many students choose a field at eighteen simply because of their grades, and then change their major after a year, which wastes far more time than a planned break. Moreover, working or volunteering teaches responsibility and independence. Students who have managed their own money or helped in a community project usually arrive at university more mature and more motivated. In Israel, for instance, students who start university after military service and a period of travel are often more focused than younger students abroad. It is true that a gap year postpones a career by twelve months. However, over a working life of forty years, this delay is minor compared with the benefits of making a wiser choice.

wr.prompt: Some people claim that social media does more harm than good, especially to young people. Others argue that it brings important benefits. Write a response in which you state your opinion and support it with reasons and examples.
tips: הימנעו מתשובה קיצונית מדי (״social media destroys everything״) – עמדה מאוזנת אך ברורה נשמעת אקדמית יותר.
דוגמאות טובות: השוואה חברתית ודימוי עצמי מול שמירה על קשר עם חברים ומשפחה, או למידה וקהילות תמיכה.
הקפידו על התאמה בין נושא לנשוא (social media has / young people have) – טעות נפוצה בנושא הזה.
wr.model: In my opinion, social media does more harm than good for young people, although it does have some benefits. The greatest danger is its effect on self-esteem. Teenagers constantly see edited photos of their friends' perfect lives, and many begin to feel that their own lives are boring or unsuccessful. Several studies have linked heavy use of these platforms to anxiety and poor sleep. In addition, social media is designed to keep users scrolling, which leaves less time for homework, sports and real conversations. Admittedly, these platforms can also be positive. They help young people stay in touch with relatives abroad and find communities that share their interests. However, these advantages could be achieved with far less time online. Therefore, I believe that young people should limit their use of social media, and schools should teach them to use it more wisely.

wr.prompt: In some countries, university education is free for all citizens, while in others students must pay high tuition fees. Some people believe that higher education should be free for everyone. Write a response in which you state your opinion and support it with reasons and examples.
tips: הגדירו לעצמכם לפני הכתיבה שלושה מרכיבים: עמדה, שתי סיבות, ותגובה לטיעון נגד אחד. זה כל המבנה שצריך.
דוגמאות שימושיות: מדינות שבהן הלימודים חינם (כמו גרמניה), חובות סטודנטים, שוויון הזדמנויות.
השתמשו במבנים שמראים רמה: If..., ...would; Not only... but also; Although....
wr.model: I believe that university education should be free, or at least very cheap, for all citizens. Firstly, free education creates equal opportunities. Talented students from poor families often give up on university because they cannot afford the fees, and society loses their potential. Secondly, highly educated citizens benefit the whole country, not only themselves. Doctors, engineers and teachers contribute to the economy and pay higher taxes throughout their lives. Germany, for example, offers free university education and still has one of the strongest economies in Europe. Opponents argue that free education is a heavy burden on taxpayers and may lead students to take their studies less seriously. Although this concern is understandable, it could be addressed by requiring students to pass their courses in order to keep their free place. In short, free higher education is not a gift but a long-term investment in the nation's future.

wr.prompt: Some schools have banned students from using smartphones during the school day, including during breaks. Supporters say this improves concentration, while opponents say students need their phones. Write a response in which you state your opinion and support it with reasons and examples.
tips: שימו לב לפרט בפרומפט – האיסור כולל גם הפסקות. התייחסו אליו במפורש: האם האיסור בהפסקות מוצדק?
אפשר להציע פתרון ביניים (טלפונים בלוקר, שימוש רק בשעת חירום), אבל אמרו בבירור אם אתם בעד האיסור או נגדו.
בדקו בסוף שהמונה בטווח 100–150 ושכל משפט מסתיים בנקודה – משפטים ארוכים ורצים זה בזה הם טעות נפוצה.
wr.model: I support banning smartphones during the school day, including breaks. The main reason is concentration. When a phone is on the desk, students are tempted to check messages every few minutes, and even a short interruption makes it harder to follow a lesson. Teachers in schools with such bans often report that students pay more attention and participate more actively. The ban during breaks is also important. Without phones, students talk to each other, play games outside and make new friends, instead of sitting silently in front of their screens. Opponents claim that students need phones to contact their parents in an emergency. However, this problem can easily be solved: phones can be kept in a locker and used with a teacher's permission, and parents can always call the school office. For these reasons, I believe a full ban benefits both learning and social life.
